title: Wet rock below the water table
question: One of these darkens every rock cell below the column's own water table. Which is the ground you would rather stand on?
context_md:
Both sides already have the six-rock vocabulary; the only difference is the damp family. It is one byte written at genesis -- family 0 multiplied by (0.78, 0.79, 0.83), because a water film kills the diffuse scatter off the grain and loses least at the blue end -- so it costs nothing per frame and nothing per cell after genesis.

**It is the largest single thing in the proposal by pixels and it is the one I am least sure of.** On its own it moves 19.5% of the viewport -- more than the whole `soil_blanket` pass -- and it moves exactly **0 pixels on arid**, which has no water table at all. But it also *reduces* the number of colours covering half the ground on three of five presets, because it pulls a very large area toward one value. That is the trade I cannot judge by measuring: real wet ground, or a world with the lights turned down.

items.label: damp below the table
items.caption: rock at or below ColumnPlan::table_y takes the damp family
